title: LivePage into Page: the plan
description: Where LivePage's 1,220 lines go: into Page, into reusable views, or into plugins. Waits for your yes.

add.text:
**The plan in one line:** every page becomes live through its store, and LivePage's extras become plugins a page can turn on or off. LivePage itself goes away. **Nothing is built or merged until you say yes.**

![Where LivePage's lines go: Page ~200, reusable views ~330, plugins ~390, the store ~50, card types ~270](./where.svg)

add.title: Plugins: one system, already built
add.description: core/Plugin already does all of it, per instance included: `page.plugins.set({tabs: {enabled: false}})` turns tabs off on one page only. Page doesn't use it yet: it has its own `Page.use`, `page.ext()` and `{"ext": …}`, three hooks with no on/off.
add.text:
**Built today in core/Plugin:** `Host.use(A)`, `Host.unuse(A)`, the `Host.plugins` rows (`enabled`, `config`), and **per instance**: `inst.plugins.set({A: {enabled: false}})`, `inst.overrides` (plain data, saveable), `Host.make_default(inst)`.

**Page today:** `Item extends Events(Object)`, not Plugin. Page has its own `Page.use(Ext)` (nobody calls it), `page.ext(name)` and a `{"ext": "Inbox"}` line. That is three ways to add a feature and none can be switched off.

**Decision:** turn Plugin into a mixin, `Pluggable(Base)` (the way `Events(Base)` works), and write `class Page extends Pluggable(Item)`. The three old hooks become plugin rows, and their names stay as aliases. A page's own choice is one line in its store, `{"plugins": {"tabs": {"enabled": false}}}`, which the item tool and the gear page both write.

**Alternative:** `Item extends Plugin`, so every Item, Task and Session is pluggable. It wins if tasks need plugins too; the cost is tracking every item. Start with Page and widen later.

add.title: The shape (proposal, not built)
add.caption: The namespaces proposal and the plugin system become one: each group (tabs, columns, previews, log) is a plugin.

add.title: Where each part of LivePage goes
add.description: Page itself gets the render with its error box, sub-page routing and links (~200 lines). Reusable views get the header and the cards (~330). Plugins get tabs, settings, status, sub-pages, tasks, voice and buttons (~390).
add.text:
| LivePage part (lines) | Goes to | Why |
|---|---|---|
| render, body, error box (`caught`, `safely`) ~80 | **Page** | every page should show what failed |
| sub-page routing (`child`, `route`, `folder`) ~50, links (`follow`, `link_url`) ~25 | **Page** | Page already has `child()` and `link()`; LivePage's versions replace them |
| Head, Crumbs, Focus, Foot ~130 | **view** `core/Page/PageHead.js` | the header the owner liked: breadcrumb, icon, title, gear |
| Main, Items, Card, Block, Preview, Heading, Md ~180 | **views** in `core/Page/parts/` | Card and Block keep their API |
| storage icons ~30 | **view** | dot = embedded, file = own .jsonl, folder = own folder |
| Tabs + `tabs_of` ~95 | **plugin** `tabs` | merged with ext/tabs (below) |
| Settings + Files ~80 | **plugin** `settings` | the gear page; reuses `core/Page/FilesTab.js` |
| Status, Errors, `flash`, `alert` ~80 | **plugin** `status` | |
| Pages, Children ~50 | **plugin** `pages` | merged with `core/Page/Children.js` |
| Tasks ~20 | **plugin** `tasks` | the session page needs it first |
| `listen`, `paint_voice` ~35 | **plugin** `voice` | |
| `save`, `restore`, `can_press` ~35 | **plugin** `buttons` | |
| `meta_of`, `meta_stream` ~50 | **the store** | watching a sub-page's own title is the store's job, not Page's |
| LiveChecklist, LiveLight, LiveButton, LiveCode, LiveContent ~270 | **card types** | already registered; unchanged |

add.title: Page's methods: half can leave, Item is already lean
add.description: Three rankers (Haiku, Sonnet, mine) agree on 119 of 196 methods. All three move 61 out of Page (tabs, columns, previews, logs, files, markdown, JSONL hooks); Item keeps almost all of its own.
add.text:
**How:** a script listed every method of `Page.class.js` (131) and `Item.js` (65). Haiku and Sonnet ranked them independently as core, secondary or move-out; my ranking is written as rules ([opus-rules.mjs](/framework/ai/sessions/2026/11/06/spawned/mastermind-live-page/live-plan/opus-rules.mjs)), and the comparison is computed ([compare.json](/framework/ai/sessions/2026/11/06/spawned/mastermind-live-page/live-plan/compare.json)).

| | Haiku | Sonnet | Mine |
|---|---|---|---|
| core / secondary / move-out | 60 / 59 / 77 | 75 / 54 / 67 | 58 / 47 / 91 |
| Page methods to move out | 75 of 131 | 64 of 131 | 77 of 131 |
| Item methods to move out | 2 of 65 | 3 of 65 | 14 of 65 |

- **All three agree on 119 of 196** (pairs agree on 140 to 144).
- **Core, all three:** 40, e.g. `set`, `get`, `lists`, `pages`, `child`, `render`, `activate`, `replay`, `toJSON`, `open`.
- **Move out, all three:** 61, e.g. every `tab_*`, `column_*`, `preview_*`, `log_*`, `md_*`, the JSONL hooks (`file`, `child_file`, `link_child`), `prefs`, and the deprecated `children`.
- Most of these are already one-line forwarders to helper classes (`Jsonl.js`, `Columns.js`, `Previews.js`), so moving them out is mostly deleting the forwarder and naming the helper as a plugin.
- ⚠ Haiku's own summary said 86 core; its rows say 60. The rows are right, so the counts here are computed, not taken from the summary.

Files: [haiku](/framework/ai/sessions/2026/11/06/spawned/mastermind-live-page/live-plan/rank-haiku.tsv) · [sonnet](/framework/ai/sessions/2026/11/06/spawned/mastermind-live-page/live-plan/rank-sonnet.tsv) · [mine](/framework/ai/sessions/2026/11/06/spawned/mastermind-live-page/live-plan/rank-opus.tsv)

add.title: The one real disagreement: who fetches a file
add.description: Both minions call Item's `file_url`, `load` and `root_from` core. I'd move them to the store, because that is what keeps Page and Item store-agnostic. Decide this one first.
add.text:
Haiku and Sonnet rank `Item.file_url`, `Item.load` and `Item.root_from` as **core**: an item knows how to fetch its own file. I rank them **move-out** to the store (`core/Item/Store.js`). If an item builds a `.jsonl` url, the store can't become a Durable Object without editing Item.

**My call:** an Item keeps `Item.open(url)`, and how its lines arrive belongs to the store. Page's 343-line `Jsonl.js` helper moves behind the store the same way. **Alternative:** leave them in Item and accept that a second store means editing Item; that wins only if JSONL stays the only store.

add.title: Duplicates, settled
add.description: Tabs: three today (ext/tabs, Page's tab lines, LivePage.Tabs), one tabs plugin after. Question: a task and a view with the same name; the view is renamed. Prompt: the chat Prompt is the one, as its own note already says.
add.text:
**Tabs (three today):**
- `ext/tabs`: `this.tabs()`, 143 lines, 22 importers, and ext/Doc's top tabs are this.
- Page's own tab state: `{"tab": …}` lines in `Jsonl.js` and `navigation: "tabs"`.
- `LivePage.Tabs`: ~95 lines with its scroll fade and its row of sub-pages.

After: **one `tabs` plugin.** Its data is Page's `tab` lines, its view is ext/tabs's bar with LivePage's fade and row folded in, and `this.tabs()` stays as the alias ext/Doc calls.

**Question (two):** `core/Task/Question.js` (a Task: the data) and `ux/Content/Question/Question.js` (a ContentModule: a field and a button that writes an `answer` line). One is the thing, the other draws it. Keep the Task as the one `Question` and rename the view `QuestionView`, which draws a Question task. 1 or 2 importers each.

**Prompt (two):** `core/Task/Prompt.js` (a Task, registered as "Prompt", read by chat v2 and v3) and `core/Session/Chat/Prompt.js` (a chat Message). The second one's header already says it is the target and the Task Prompt retires. Follow that note: the chat Prompt becomes the one when chat v3 reads messages. `ai/AITask/prompt.js` is a text helper, not a class, so it isn't a duplicate.

add.title: First adopter: the session page
add.description: The session page becomes `Page` with the head, tasks and status plugins over `Session.open(url)`, about 40 lines. It proves the plugins on a real page before LivePage changes at all.
add.text:
Today `AISessionDetail` (648 lines) draws its own head and tabs and reads `session.jsonl` with four JSONL readers ([the study](/live/session-page/)).

After: `class SessionPage extends Page` with `Head`, `Tasks` and `Status` turned on. Its tasks appear, start and close live (the live tail already works, 9782b2db5). The old tabs (Timeline, Cost, …) stay one click away. The voice chat (Dictate) adopts the same plugins next, so the three surfaces converge on one record.

add.title: Page stays store-agnostic
add.description: No JSONL code in Page. Page asks the store for an item and its changes; JSONL is today's store and a Durable Object could be tomorrow's. The JSONL hooks and LivePage's meta reader move behind the store.
add.text:
- Page and its plugins speak only in items and deltas: `Item.open(url)`, `item.set(delta)`, and a change event.
- The store turns that into files: today `page.jsonl` and the `live()` tail; later maybe a Durable Object with the same three calls.
- What moves behind the store: Page's `Jsonl.js` hooks (`file`, `child_file`, `link_child`, `static jsonl`), LivePage's `meta_stream`, and the session page's four readers.

add.title: After your yes: seven small steps, about $45
add.description: Each step is a worktree, a review and a smoke test, and nothing visible changes until step 3. The first: `Pluggable` on Page (~$4).
add.text:
1. **`Pluggable(Base)` mixin; `class Page extends Pluggable(Item)`.** `Page.use`, `page.ext()` and `{"ext"}` become plugin rows, with aliases kept. ~$4
2. **The header view** out of LivePage into `core/Page/PageHead.js`; LivePage uses it unchanged. ~$5
3. **The session page** on head, tasks and status plugins (the first adopter). ~$5
4. **One tabs plugin**, merging the three. ~$8
5. **The settings plugin** (the gear page) over `FilesTab.js`. ~$5
6. **Status and content views** into core/Page; Card and Block keep their API. ~$8
7. **Page's 61 agreed move-outs** become plugin parts (a scripted rename with a dry run, per namespaces.md); LivePage becomes `Page` plus a plugin list and is kept as an alias. ~$10

add.title: The alternatives
add.description: Merge LivePage into Page whole (fast, but Page doubles in size and nothing can be switched off). Or keep LivePage as a template class on top of Page (no core change, but two page systems stay).
add.text:
- **Merge LivePage into Page whole:** one big step, but Page grows by ~950 lines and every page pays for every feature. It loses the owner's "keep Page small and predictable".
- **LivePage stays a template (`class LivePage extends Page`):** no core risk, but two page systems remain and the session page and voice chat can't share its parts. That breaks "one of everything".
- **Chosen:** plugins on Page, with the session page first, because each step is small, can be undone, and is visible.

description: Where LivePage's 1,220 lines go: into Page, into reusable views, or into plugins. Approved 2026-11-09; building in small merges.

tip.text:
**The plan in one line:** every page becomes live through its store, and LivePage's extras become plugins a page can turn on or off. LivePage itself goes away.

**Status:** ✅ Step 1 merged (file loading moved from Item into the Store; [see it working](/live/item-test/)). ⬜ Step 2 building (Page takes plugins). ⬜ Then the session view, then the Page trim.

add.title: Design note: auto scroll (not built)
add.text:
Your ideas, 2026-11-09. Nothing changes until you've thought it through.

- **Rename** "scroll lock" to **auto scroll**.
- **Normal pages open at the top**, always. A first load never jumps.
- **Auto scroll is an optional plugin.** It switches on or off in a page's settings, or with one JSONL line on the page.
- **It may only act when a live update adds something at the bottom.** If you've scrolled up, it shows a "jump to bottom" link instead of moving you.
- **Chat-like pages turn it on.** The Chat class switches it on for itself, so a chat or a log still follows new lines.

It fits step 2: once Page takes plugins, auto scroll is one plugin row that a page can switch on (`page.plugins`), on by default for Chat.
